outcomes: Improved forecasts of fire-conducive weather, especially during Santa Ana events, with several days of advance notice. Operational enhancements, like temporarily disabling trunk lines in vulnerable areas, reducing the chance of equipment sparking fires. Cost savings, through avoided damages, reduced outages, and fewer wildfire ignitions linked to power infrastructure. Enhanced public safety, thanks to earlier alerts and better-prepared firefighters and utility staff

summary: In San Diego, CA, San Diego Gas & Electric Wildfire Strategy is a monitoring and adaptive management initiative. The program used inter-organizational collaboration between SDG&E, UCLA, and the U.S. Forest Service a multidisciplinary tool was developed to aid in wildfire response and mitigation: Santa Ana Wildfire Threat Index. The case addresses wildfire and Smoke. Available materials report improved forecasts of fire-conducive weather, especially during Santa Ana events, with several days of advance notice. Operational enhancements, like temporarily disabling trunk lines in vulnerable areas, reducing the chance of equipment sparking fires. Cost savings, through avoided damages, reduced outages, and fewer wildfire ignitions linked to power infrastructure. Enhanced public safety, thanks to earlier alerts and better-prepared firefighters and utility staff.
title: San Diego Gas & Electric Wildfire Strategy
transferability: This case study highlights the critical role of early warning systems and localized risk forecasting, while demonstrating how public–private partnerships and collaboration with academic institutions can drive innovative, science-based solutions. It also reinforces Washington’s commitment to proactive risk management rather than reactive emergency responses.
